summary: Bing Chen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He became a professor at Sichuan University around 1987 and was attested as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences in 1993.

Bingtao Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed an MA at Peking University in 2008 and earned his PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha worked in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and Harvard University (AM 1920, PhD 1924), he served as Director of the Anthropological Survey of India (1945–1954).

Birgit Kellner works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. She held positions at the University of Vienna and Heidelberg University, and became Director at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 2015.
Biscoe Hale Wortham was an Indology scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1863), and completed his BA at Trinity College, Oxford (1863–1868).

Bisheshwar Nath Reu worked in Indology and archaeology, having studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha (~1909–1914). From around 1916 to 1950, he headed the Government Museum Jodhpur and served as Superintendent at the Sumer Public Library.
Biswajit Biswas specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and served as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Biswanath Banerjee was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991. He was also a former president of The Asiatic Society (attested circa 2002–2004).
Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (2002–2009) and was appointed professor at the University of Lausanne in 2013.
Blanche Christine Olschak was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Graz (~1933–1937) and studied under Constantin Régamey and Thupten Wangyal in 1946.
Bo Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas is an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. Educated at Uppsala University (~1958–1972) under Stig Wikander and Henrik Samuel Nyberg, he served there as professor emeritus (~1987–2003).
Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Silwon Suk. He served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested in 2004 and 2015).
Bohumil Sládeček was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts (~1903–1918), completing his PhD under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý by 1918.

Bojan Čop was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Ljubljana under Karel Oštir, earning a PhD, and served there as full Professor of Comparative IE linguistics from 1972 to 1990.

Bokar Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989). He held a post at Bokar Monastery (~1984–2004) and taught disciples including Shenpen Hookham and Ogyen Trinley Dorje.
Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned his PhD at Princeton University under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and served as a professor of philosophy at Florida International University (attested 1991–1992, 2012).

Borayin Larios is an Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and Heidelberg University. He held posts at Heidelberg, the University of Vienna (2018), and headed a department at the French Institute of Pondicherry (2023–2024).

Boris Aleksandrovich Larin was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv (1910–1914) under Friedrich Knauer, and later held professorships at Saint Petersburg State University from 1922 through the 1960s.
